guidance.procedure: For each hypothesis independently align actor, modality, action, object, quantifier, trigger, conditions, exceptions and governing definitions. Silence or a neighboring topic is unresolved; never infer permission from absence, a trigger from mere survival, or one relationship from another. Select every original member needed to express the governing rule, operative clause, exception or independently responsive repetition. Exclude headings, recitals, certifications and merely adjacent provisions.

Separate the disposition trigger from its remedy. A request-only clause does not establish disposition at agreement end; completion, discontinued dealings or termination must be linked to return or destruction. Because “some” is existential, disposition of a covered subset supports even if another subset may be kept. Retention requires an affirmative archive, backup, recordkeeping or similar carve-out; an all-copies or no-retention command opposes it. Cite the trigger, remedy and operative carve-out when jointly controlling.

Support survival only when an identified obligation expressly continues after termination, has a post-termination period, or remains binding for retained material. A term provision, possible later end date or generic survival exception without a continuing duty is insufficient. Cite each independently responsive continuing obligation, not a generic term clause substituted for it.

Resolve definition hypotheses from all alternative inclusion routes. Express nontechnical categories oppose technical-only coverage; do not treat a technical example as an exclusive definition. Oral coverage requires an express oral, verbal or spoken route, not an inference from broad information language or unspecified form. Universal identification fails when content, circumstances, implication or an automatic category can qualify information without designation, marking or notice. Cite the governing introduction and each operative route needed to show the boundary.

Independent development requires an express permission or exclusion for development by the receiving party; development or disclosure by other actors does not substitute, and silence remains unresolved. Third-party acquisition requires an express lawful or nonconfidential-source route, with any no-duty or authorization conditions preserved. Cite the governing exclusion introduction plus the responsive subclause, including independently repeated definitions.

Require an operative standing permission to disclose to the relevant class, together with need-to-know, purpose or confidentiality conditions. A definition of representatives alone is not permission. Prior-consent-only language or a blanket third-party ban opposes sharing under this annotation convention; silence is unresolved. Evaluate employees separately from consultants, agents, advisers and other nonemployees, and cite both the class definition and operative permission when both govern.

A no-rights or no-license clause, reserved ownership, or exclusive-property provision supports no-license. Permission to receive, evaluate, use or disclose information does not itself grant a proprietary right and does not oppose no-license. A positive license must cover the confidential information or its rights; a license concerning separate marks, products or services is not responsive. Cite independent ownership and reservation provisions when each is annotated as governing.

A prohibition on revealing the agreement’s existence, exchanged material, discussions, negotiations, terms, conditions or status supports agreement confidentiality; keep its polarity as support for the prohibitory hypothesis. A confidentiality duty covering only substantive information, an enforcement notice, or an entire-agreement clause does not settle this issue. Preserve separately operative listed aspects as evidence members.

Require a restriction on soliciting, hiring, inducing or recruiting the disclosing party’s employees, officers or other representatives. Restrictions on contacting customers, suppliers, business sources, transaction counterparties or designated contacts do not substitute, nor does a general noncompete. Preserve scope limitations and recruiting or general-advertisement exceptions without treating them as elimination of the operative restriction.

Copy permission requires an affirmative operative allowance; do not infer it from silence or from a qualification within a reproduction ban. An express copying, reproduction or retention prohibition opposes copy permission, while an express exception supports it. Reverse-engineering restrictions require that act or functionally specified disassembly or decompilation; ordinary copying and use limits are insufficient. Absolute design, development or manufacture use bans can support reverse-engineering when they functionally cover that conduct.

Require an affirmative notice duty tied to disclosure compelled by law, regulation, subpoena, judicial process or governmental demand. Notice of an unauthorized breach is not responsive. Preserve qualifications such as legal permission, practicability and advance timing. Cite the governing compelled-disclosure exception, the notice command, and any linked opportunity-to-object language that independently defines the duty.

Support limited use only from an operative restriction tying use of confidential information to stated, agreed, evaluation or transaction purposes. A nondisclosure rule, a limit on what information may be requested, or a restriction concerning separate marks or products does not substitute. Cite independently operative repetitions and any governing introduction that supplies the protected object or permitted purpose.

For each hypothesis independently align actor, modality, action, object, quantifier, trigger, conditions and exceptions before selecting evidence. Silence and neighboring topics are unresolved; never infer permission from absence, a trigger from survival, or one relationship from another. Select every original member independently expressing the governing rule, responsive repetition, necessary scope or operative exception. Headings, recitals and consequences are not members merely by proximity, but retain them when they actually supply a governing object, purpose, condition or responsive proposition.

operations.rationale: Observed errors repeatedly substituted adjacent subjects and either dropped governing members or cited nonresponsive context.

guidance.procedure: Classify the disposition trigger separately from the remedy. Return or destruction supports termination disposition only when linked to termination, expiration, completion, abandonment, non-pursuit or an equivalent end of dealings; a request-only duty is unresolved. Because “some” is existential, disposition of any covered subset suffices. For retention, an affirmative archive, backup, legal-file, recordkeeping or document-policy carve-out supports possession, while exhaustive return or destruction, all-copies language or an express no-retention command opposes it. Never treat the existence of a return duty as retention permission. Cite the operative trigger and remedy for disposition; for retention cite the carve-out introduction and each independently retained category, without importing unrelated alternatives.

operations.rationale: The answers often treated requests as termination triggers and reversed the polarity of retention and no-retention clauses.

guidance.procedure: Find an identified duty that continues beyond termination, expiration or another stated endpoint. Support survival from express continuation, a post-termination duration, an indefinite confidentiality period, retained material remaining subject to duties, or provisions remaining effective after another restriction ends. A contract term, possible later end date, remedies for a prior breach or a generic exception lacking a continuing duty is insufficient. Cite every independently responsive continuation, including bilateral or repeated provisions and any short connector needed to identify what continues; do not substitute an ordinary term clause.

operations.rationale: Relations were usually correct, but continuing duties, retained-material clauses and repeated survival provisions were frequently omitted.

guidance.procedure: Resolve each definition boundary from every operative inclusion route. Technical-only coverage requires an exhaustive definition confined to technical or comparable system categories; business, financial, personal, commercial or other nontechnical categories oppose it, while an isolated example or unrelated information reference does not decide it. Oral coverage requires a governing route for oral, verbal, spoken, visual, intangible, any-medium or not-reduced-to-writing disclosures, not merely the word “information.” Universal identification is supported only when every route requires designation, marking, notice or equivalent identification; it is opposed when content, circumstances, implication, absence of marking or another automatic route can qualify information. A broad definition without either condition may remain unresolved. Cite the governing introduction and all alternative routes necessary to establish the boundary, excluding merely illustrative or adjacent lists.

operations.rationale: The model confused broad definitions with technical-only or oral coverage and failed to aggregate alternative identification routes.

guidance.procedure: For independent development, require an express exclusion or permission for development, creation or discovery by the receiving party, including qualifying pre-disclosure creation or an affirmative allowance for future competing development. Development or disclosure solely by other actors does not substitute, and a use restriction does not oppose independent development unless it reaches independently created information. For third-party acquisition, require a lawful, authorized or nonconfidential third-party source route and preserve its no-duty, knowledge and authorization conditions. Cite the governing exclusion introduction plus each responsive route, including repeated bilateral definitions or separately operative similar-information permissions; do not select an entire exclusions block merely because one subclause qualifies.

operations.rationale: Frequent misses involved exclusion introductions, bilateral repetitions and actor-specific development or third-party conditions.

guidance.procedure: Require an operative standing permission or exception allowing disclosure or access to the relevant class, subject to any need-to-know, purpose, written-undertaking or confidentiality conditions. A representatives definition alone is not permission. For nonemployee third parties, confirm that the permitted class expressly includes consultants, contractors, agents, advisers or another nonemployee category; an undefined generic representative label is insufficient by itself. Evaluate employees separately. A blanket ban on disclosure to any person or third party, or prior-consent-only disclosure, opposes sharing under this annotation convention and may cover employees even when unnamed. Cite the operative permission or ban and any class definition needed to resolve scope; exclude responsibility, breach and security clauses that add no permission.

operations.rationale: The model conflated employees with external representatives and treated bans, definitions and responsibility clauses as permissions.

guidance.procedure: Support no-license from an express no-rights or no-license rule, retained or exclusive ownership, or a property reservation covering confidential information or its intellectual-property rights. Cite every independently operative ownership and reservation provision, including bilateral counterparts, when each governs the protected information. Permission to receive, evaluate, use or disclose information is not a proprietary grant and does not oppose no-license. A license concerning separate marks, products or services is nonresponsive. Oppose no-license only when an affirmative license actually reaches the confidential information or its associated rights; silence remains unresolved.

operations.rationale: Recent answers missed independently annotated ownership provisions and bilateral no-rights repetitions.

guidance.procedure: Require an operative restriction on publicizing or disclosing the agreement’s existence, a confidential relationship, exchanged material, discussions, negotiations, transaction status, terms, conditions or related facts. A prior-consent qualification remains a prohibition and supports the prohibitory hypothesis. An NDA title, heading, generic substantive-information duty, enforcement notice or entire-agreement clause does not settle this issue. Cite the governing prohibition and every separately operative listed aspect; include an exception only when needed to define the restriction’s scope.

operations.rationale: The model used a title as evidence in one contract and missed operative publicity and confidential-relationship restrictions in others.

guidance.procedure: Require a restriction on soliciting, hiring, offering to hire, inducing, recruiting or encouraging departure by the disclosing party’s employees, officers, agents or other representatives. Restrictions limited to customers, suppliers, vendors, business sources, transaction counterparties or designated contacts do not substitute, nor does a general noncompete. Cite the governing restriction and every relevant target subclause or bilateral repetition, while excluding adjacent customer, supplier and business-source restrictions. Preserve duration, contact-level limitations and recruiting or general-advertisement exceptions only when they define the operative employee restriction.

operations.rationale: The model confused business-source solicitation with representative solicitation and omitted repeated employee classes.

guidance.procedure: Copy permission requires an affirmative allowance or an operative exception permitting copies in stated circumstances; an exception within a copying prohibition can therefore support limited permission. A copying, reproduction or duplication prohibition opposes permission. References to notices appearing on copies, existing retained copies or backup retention do not themselves authorize creating copies. Reverse-engineering support requires that act or functionally specified disassembly, decompilation or equivalent extraction; ordinary copying and use limits are insufficient, though an absolute design, development or manufacture ban may functionally cover the conduct. Cite any governing no-consent introduction together with the responsive act, and exclude adjacent media or retention details.

operations.rationale: The model inverted limited-copy exceptions, inferred permission from copy references and omitted governing language for reverse-engineering bans.

guidance.procedure: Require an affirmative notice duty tied to disclosure compelled by law, regulation, subpoena, judicial process or governmental demand. Notice of an unauthorized breach is not responsive. Preserve legal-permission, practicability and advance-timing qualifications. Cite a governing compelled-disclosure introduction when it supplies the trigger or protected object, the notice command, and any separately operative opportunity-to-object language defining the notice’s purpose. Do not cite later minimum-disclosure, authorization, cooperation or confidential-treatment steps unless they independently impose or qualify notice; include bilateral repetitions when each creates the duty.

operations.rationale: Answers often omitted governing triggers or objection opportunities while adding later disclosure mechanics unrelated to notice.

guidance.procedure: Support limited use only when an operative rule ties use of the protected information to a stated, agreed, evaluation, transaction or proper-performance purpose, forbids every other purpose, or expressly treats unauthorized or unlicensed reuse as prohibited. Match the actor and protected object: nondisclosure alone, limits on information requests, assignment language, or restrictions concerning separate marks, products or services do not substitute. Scan distinct protected categories and repeated provisions, and cite every independently operative purpose restriction plus any governing introduction supplying the object or permitted purpose; exclude neighboring disclosure clauses unless they also restrict use.

operations.rationale: Purpose restrictions were frequently missed across repeated categories, while unrelated disclosure, request, assignment and mark clauses were cited.
